content.title: About
content.content: Rosé wine is a light, semi‑sweet wine made from red grape varieties with a short skin contact period. It features a fresh fruit aroma with notes of strawberry, raspberry and citrus, balanced by a crisp acidity.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Rosé gets its characteristic pink hue, ranging from pale blush to bright ruby, depending on grape variety and winemaking technique.
The modern rosé style originated in Provence, France, in the 19th century.
Unlike red wine, rosé is usually fermented at cooler temperatures, preserving delicate aromatic compounds.
Rosé is typically served chilled (8–12 °C) to highlight its fruitiness.
There are several rosé styles: dry, off‑dry, semi‑sweet and dessert rosés.

items.title: Antioxidants
items.content: Rosé contains polyphenols such as resveratrol, which may protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Cardiovascular support
items.content: Moderate rosé consumption (about 150 ml per day) is linked to improved lipid profiles and reduced heart disease risk.

items.title: Gut microbiota support
items.content: Fermented beverages can contribute to a diverse intestinal microbiome.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Rosé provides small amounts of B1, B2 and B6 vitamins involved in energy metabolism.

items.title: Hydration
items.content: Its high water content helps maintain fluid balance when consumed in moderation.

items.title: Alcohol
items.content: Excessive alcohol intake can cause liver damage, dependence, and other health issues.

items.title: Sulfite sensitivity
items.content: Some wines contain sulfites, which may trigger allergic reactions in sensitive individuals.

items.title: Medication interactions
items.content: Alcohol can amplify the effects of certain drugs, including anticoagulants and diabetes medications.

items.title: Pregnancy
items.content: Pregnant women are advised to limit or avoid alcohol.

items.title: Caloric content
items.content: Rosé provides roughly 80–90 kcal per 100 ml, which should be considered in weight management.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve rosé chilled in medium‑sized glasses. It pairs well with light appetizers, salads, seafood, grilled chicken, and soft cheeses. Rosé can also be used in cooking for marinades and sauces.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the bottle in a cool, dark place away from direct sunlight. Once opened, reseal and store in the refrigerator for up to 3–5 days.
